hook: One question every five year old needs for AI pictures
book_line: Real or pretend. A few minutes, on the sofa.

ask1: Can you think of something on a screen that is PRETEND? And something that is REAL?
There is no wrong answer. Let it land.
ask2: When we are not sure... we ASK.
Then give each other a high five.

child.text: Hello, it's Didgee. And here's Pebble.
Oh, Pebble. Other way round. That's better.
Let's breathe together. Breathe in, and blow out slowly. One more. Lovely.
Last time, we learned that a photo only shows a tiny bit of you. Today, we're picture detectives.
Today's special word is pretend.
Pretend means made up. Not really happening.
Some things are real. A real puppy. Real rain. Real splashes.
Some things are pretend. Dragons are pretend. Someone drew this one, to make a story.
And here's a tricky one. A computer can make a picture of something that never happened.
This dog never went to the moon. A computer made the picture. It looks real, but it isn't.
Sometimes you can't tell, just by looking. And that's okay. You don't have to know by yourself.
Pause me here, and ask each other the question. I'll wait.
So when you're not sure, ask the magic question.
Is this real?
Take it to your grown up and ask: is this real? Then look at it together.
Let's play. Real, pretend, or made by a computer? Shout it out.
The puppy in the puddle?
Real!
The dragon?
Pretend!
The dog on the moon?
Made by a computer. Ooh, tricky.
The clever thing isn't knowing. The clever thing is asking.
Pause me here. Say it together, and do your high five.
You will never be in trouble for asking. Grown ups love that question.
So. Some things are real. Some are pretend. And some are made by a computer.
And if you're not sure, ask. Is this real?
Tonight, if you see something amazing on a screen, ask your grown up: is this real?
Goodbye from Didgee. See you next time.

parent.text: This dog never went to the moon. A computer made the picture, in seconds.
Sometimes nobody can tell just by looking. Not your child, and not us.

parent.big: Don't teach them to spot the fakes. Teach them to ask.
parent.text: So don't teach them to spot the fakes. Teach them to ask.
The magic question is: is this real?

parent.eye: The answer that keeps them asking
parent.text: And the answer that keeps them asking: good question, let's look together.
Real or pretend is a few minutes on the sofa. In Guided Childhood you can book a time, and it waits on their page then.
Tonight, when something amazing turns up on a screen, ask together: is this real?
